Fact.Description: Whether the return attaches Schedule 2. It is the render gate the schedule needs in dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv and the MeF attachment signal. The schedule has two printed parts and this gate reads a signal from each: Part I through the line 1a excess-APTC repayment, the line 1b/1c clean vehicle credit dealer-transfer repayment and the line 2 alternative minimum tax; Part II through the line 21 total ("Add lines 4, 7 through 16, 18, and 19"), which is what a return owing self-employment tax, additional Medicare tax, net investment income tax, household employment taxes or any of the Part II excise and recapture lines carries to Form 1040 line 23. A return whose only Schedule 2 content is Part II attaches the schedule, and so does one whose only Schedule 2 content is a Part I entry line the three named items do not cover: the line 1d Form 4255 net elective payment election recapture and the open line 1y additions to tax both reach line 3.

Schedule 2 line 1a ("Excess advance premium tax credit repayment. Attach Form 8962"): in scope the excess-APTC repayment (Form 8962 line 29 = /lesserOfNetPtcAmountAndRepaymentLimitation), 0 unless the PTC net amount is negative and a repayment limitation applies. Split out from /line1zOfSchedule2 when line 1z gained the clean-vehicle dealer-transfer repayment terms (lines 1b/1c) and is NO LONGER equal to line 1a, so a consumer whose limit is stated on line 1a ALONE — the foreign tax credit no-Form-1116 cap, "line 16 + Schedule 2 line 1a" — must reference this fact, never the full 1z subtotal. Complete-safe: resolves 0 when no excess-APTC repayment applies. NOT mef-exported by design: line 1z (/line1zOfSchedule2, which includes this) carries the MeF/spine Schedule-2 export; line 1a was never a separate exported fact (it was inline in line 1z before that split), so keeping this internal preserves the export surface exactly — value-neutral. It may be promoted to mef="true" if MeF needs line 1a broken out.

Schedule 2 line 1z ("Add lines 1a through 1y"): the additions-to-tax subtotal. Its addends are the excess advance premium tax credit repayment (line 1a, /line1aOfSchedule2), the clean vehicle credit dealer-transfer repayments (line 1b new + line 1c used), line 1d (form4255 /form4255NetEpeRecaptureFromLine2aOrZero), line 1e (/form4255ExcessivePaymentsOnGrossEpeOrZero), line 1f (/form4255TwentyPercentExcessivePaymentOrZero) and line 1y (/schedule2Line1yOtherAdditionsToTax). Reused as the Schedule 2 line 1z term of Form 6251 line 10 (the regular tax for the AMT comparison). ⚠ line 1z ≠ line 1a: a line-1a-only consumer must use /line1aOfSchedule2. Every addend other than line 1a is complete-safe 0 when unanswered, so on a return with none of them line 1z equals line 1a.

Schedule 2 line 3 ("Add lines 1z and 2"), for Form 1040 line 17: the additions-to-tax subtotal (line 1z) plus the alternative minimum tax (line 2, Form 6251). The AMT term is 0 for every return that is not AMT-liable.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17b, recapture of federal mortgage subsidy, as line 18 adds it
Fact.Description: Form 8828 line 23 when the return owes the recapture tax (form8828 /form8828SubjectToRecaptureTax true), and $0 when it does not. Unlike the complete-safe form8828 /form8828Line23RecaptureTaxOrZero, an owed recapture whose Form 8828 Part II is not yet complete leaves this line Incomplete rather than falling back to $0, the standard lines 16, 17n, 17p, 17q and 20 already follow: an active form that is not yet complete leaves the line Incomplete, so line 18, line 21 and Form 1040 line 23 cannot file without the tax section 143(m) imposes. THE SAME RULE APPLIES the other way round: a return whose Form 8828 Part II sale figures (/form8828Line14HalfOfGain and /form8828Line22RecaptureAmount) are both answered, so a recapture amount could be computed, but whose filing-population questions (/form8828SubjectToRecaptureTax, gated on the Part I subsidy-type boxes) are not yet answered, is a return that has engaged the form without yet saying whether the tax applies at all -- it is not the ordinary return that never touches Form 8828, and $0 is not a fact about it yet. This line stays Incomplete on exactly that combination; it only falls back to the ordinary-return $0 when the Part II sale figures are ALSO unanswered, which is every return this dictionary has committed apart from that one. The worksheet ceiling for the Negative Form 8978 adjustment keeps reading the complete-safe wrapper, since line 18 is itself Incomplete on exactly the returns where the two differ.

Fact.Name: Line 18 of Schedule 2
Fact.Description: Schedule 2 (Form 1040) Part II line 18, "Total additional taxes. Add lines 17a through 17z". EVERY printed sub-line is an addend, in printed order: 17a (/schedule2Line17aRecaptureOfOtherCredits; the recapture of an education credit is NOT a line 17a amount, because the Form 1040 instructions put it on Form 1040 line 16 with box 3 checked and "ECR", where taxCalculations /otherFormEducationCreditRecapture carries it), 17b (form8828 /form8828Line23RecaptureTaxOrZero, the mortgage subsidy recapture), 17c (hsa /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal), 17d (hsa /hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax), 17e (hsa /archerMsaSchedule2Line17eAdditional20PctTax), 17f (hsa /medicareAdvantageMsaSchedule2Line17fAdditional50PctTax), 17g, 17h, 17i, 17j, 17l, 17m, 17n, 17o, 17p, 17q and 17z (the schedule2 complete-safe wrappers of the filer intakes) and 17k (formW2s /schedule2Line17kGoldenParachutePaymentsTax). Line 17k combines W-2 code K tax with the 20% tax on Form 1099-NEC box 3 payments; the printed field and this subtotal read the same combined fact. LINE 17z HAS THREE ADDENDS, not one: the filer's own catch-all entry /schedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxes and hsa /hsaPledgeSchedule2Line17zAdditional20PctTax, the IRC 223(f)(4)(A) 20% additional tax on an HSA amount pledged as security for a loan, which 17z carries because its own instruction admits "any taxes not reported elsewhere on your return or other schedules" and line 17c is tied to Form 8889's own line 16 arithmetic; and /schedule2Line17zNegativeForm8978Adjustment, the only addend of this subtotal that can be NEGATIVE, which is the printed Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet entry for line 17z and is capped so that it cannot drive the chapter 1 part of Part II below zero. The printed 17z BOX is a third fact, /schedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxesPrinted, which adds the same two: this subtotal adds the legs individually and never reads the printed-box fact, so an amount named in only one of them makes the filed schedule fail to foot. Every addend is complete-safe, so this fact resolves 0 rather than Incomplete on a return that answers nothing, and $0 on every committed scenario. THE LINE 21 TERM: taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2 reads THIS subtotal as its line 18 term and no longer reaches the four Form 8889 and Form 8853 taxes directly, so nothing double counts.

Fact.Name: The Form W-2 box 12 code Z term of the Schedule 2 line 17h section 409A floor
Fact.Description:
Round(20 percent of formW2s:/nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZ), the flat statutory term the return's Forms W-2 establish on their own, or $0 when that total does not resolve. A per-source figure only: the line 17h bound, /schedule2Line17hCombinedSection409AFloor, does not add this rounded term but takes 20 percent of the combined cents-preserving base (/schedule2Line17hW2CodeZUnroundedTotal plus the Form 1099-MISC box 15 total) and rounds once, so the two separately rounded terms cannot overstate the bound.
WHY THE GUARD IS NOT DECORATION. /nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZ is an ungated Round(CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/nqdcDeferralsOrZero)): on a return that has never opened the Form W-2 collection it is INCOMPLETE, not $0, and many committed scenarios are exactly that return. Reading it bare would make /schedule2Line17hBelowSection409AFloor Incomplete there, and /line18OfSchedule2 and /totalTax with it. The $0 arm keeps the combined floor complete-safe, and omitting a term only ever LOWERS a lower bound, which is the lawful direction: a floor that is too low lets a return file, a floor that is too high refuses a correct one.
THE DOUBLE ROUND IS NOT A DIVERGENCE. formW2s's own floor multiplies the cents-preserving CollectionSum and rounds once; this reads the whole-dollar total and rounds after. For a 1/5 multiplier the two agree for every input, because a half-cent boundary of 0.2 x S can only arise at a value of S that is itself a rounding boundary and half-up carries both the same way -- the committed w2-box12-code-z-boundary-half-dollar-rounds inputs are the worked case (1002.50 cents-exact gives 200.50 -> 201; 1003.00 whole-dollar gives 200.60 -> 201).

Fact.Name: Form W-2 box 12 code Z total, cents preserved, for the Schedule 2 line 17h floor
Fact.Description: The sum of box 12 code Z over every Form W-2 on the return, cents preserved and not rounded (formW2s /formW2s/*/nqdcDeferralsOrZero per document): the Form W-2 half of the base the section 409A 20 percent term is figured on. $0 when no Form W-2 was entered or no code Z amount was answered. /schedule2Line17hCombinedSection409AFloor adds it to the Form 1099-MISC box 15 base before the single rounding of the line.

Fact.Name: The combined section 409A floor on Schedule 2 line 17h
Fact.Description:
The statutory lower bound on Schedule 2 line 17h from both sources the printed line carries: 20 percent of the COMBINED base, the includible Form 1099-MISC box 15 total (form1099Misc /form1099MiscIncludibleNqdcTotal) plus the Form W-2 box 12 code Z total (/schedule2Line17hW2CodeZUnroundedTotal), plus the attested premium interest (form1099Misc /form1099MiscSection409APremiumInterestTotal), rounded ONCE to whole dollars.
THEY MUST ADD. Measured separately against the one printed line, the two floors would let a return with $10,000 of code Z and $10,000 of box 15 and a $2,000 entry clear both -- $2,000 is not greater than either $2,000 floor -- while IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(i)(II) prices the flat term alone at $4,000. The statute charges 20 percent of THE compensation required to be included in gross income, not 20 percent of each payer's share taken separately, so the bound is 20 percent of the sum.
ONE ROUND, ON THE TOTAL. Every input keeps its cents and only the line total rounds, as the Form 1040 instructions direct for a line figured by adding amounts. Rounding the two 20 percent terms separately can overstate the bound by $1 (box 15 $12.50 and code Z $12.50: $3 + $3 against the correct $5) and refuse a correct entry.
EVERY TERM IS COMPLETE-SAFE $0, so this is a hard $0 on every return that reports neither source, and /line18OfSchedule2 is byte identical there.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17h is below the combined section 409A floor this return's documents establish
Fact.Description:
TRUE when /schedule2Line17hCombinedSection409AFloor is GREATER than /schedule2Line17hSection409ANonqualifiedDeferredCompensation, the complete-safe reading of the filer's own line 17h entry.
WHY A FLOOR AND NOT A COMPLETENESS TEST. IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(i) makes the additional tax the SUM of an interest amount and 20 percent of the compensation included in gross income. The 20 percent term is flat and its base is the includible Form 1099-MISC box 15 total plus the Form W-2 box 12 code Z total, so it is a computable lower bound the moment either source is positive; the interest term needs the year the pay was first deferred and enters only as far as the filer attested it. A bare Not(IsComplete(...)) would ADMIT an answered $0.00 against a positive box 15 total, which is the contradictory intake this fact exists to catch.
ONE-DIRECTIONAL. A line 17h ABOVE the floor is never refused: it correctly carries interest the filer did not attest per document.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE. Both operands are complete-safe, so this is Complete false on every return that reports neither a Form 1099-MISC box 15 amount nor a Form W-2 box 12 code Z amount, which is every committed scenario, and /line18OfSchedule2 is byte identical there.
BOTH SOURCES ARE MEASURED TOGETHER. The two floors add, in /schedule2Line17hCombinedSection409AFloor, which reads formW2s /nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZ through /schedule2Line17hW2CodeZSection409AFloorOrZero. What remains, named and not silent, is that formW2s:/nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZBelowSchedule2Line17hFloor still measures its own term alone for its own box-12 knockout, and its carve-out sentence -- that a line 17h above its floor may carry "a Form 1099-MISC box 15 amount this dictionary does not total" -- is stale prose in formW2s.xml.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17h: income from a nonqualified deferred compensation plan failing section 409A (filer entry)

THE FIGURE IS STILL THE FILER'S OWN ENTRY, because the interest component of the tax is priced by IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(ii) off the year the pay was first deferred and the underpayment rate in each year since, neither of which any information return in this dictionary carries. BOTH AMOUNTS THE LINE IS FIGURED FROM ARE TOTALLED, though: formW2s /nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZ sums the Form W-2 box 12 code Z amounts, and form1099Misc /form1099MiscNonqualifiedDeferredCompensationTotal sums the Form 1099-MISC box 15 amounts. Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z, the printed amount box
Fact.Description:
The whole of printed Schedule 2 (Form 1040) line 17z, "Any other taxes. List type and amount", which is the box the PDF binds. It is the SUM of the two things this dictionary can put on that line: the filer's own catch-all entry, read complete-safely through /schedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxes, and hsa /hsaPledgeSchedule2Line17zAdditional20PctTax, the IRC 223(f)(4)(A) 20% additional tax on an HSA amount pledged as security for a loan.
IT IS SEPARATE FROM THE LINE 18 SUBTOTAL'S ADDENDS ON PURPOSE, and the separation is the fix for a defect this dictionary has already shipped once elsewhere: /line18OfSchedule2 adds every printed sub-line's legs INDIVIDUALLY and never reads a printed-box fact, so a leg named in only one of the two places prints a total that its own component box does not support. Naming the pledge tax in both is not double counting.
NO DEFAULT ARM, WHICH IS WHAT KEEPS THE BOX BLANK. A complete-safe $0 here would print "0" in the 17z box of every Schedule 2 in the corpus, where the printed form wants an empty box. This fact therefore resolves only when the filer typed an entry or the pledge tax is positive, and is Incomplete otherwise, which is the behaviour the writable it replaces on the printed line already had.
THERE ARE THREE COMPONENTS NOW, NOT TWO. The section 1294 deferred tax that has become due (form8621:/form8621DeferredTaxDue) reaches this box THROUGH /schedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxes, which already adds it, so this fact names it only in the no-default-arm gate above: the box must print when that tax alone is positive, and it would otherwise stay blank on a return whose only 17z item is the Form 8621 amount. Naming it in the gate and not in the sum is what keeps the box from double counting it.
A FOURTH COMPONENT, AND THE ONLY ONE THAT SUBTRACTS. /schedule2Line17zNegativeForm8978Adjustment is the negative entry the "Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet-Schedule 2 (Line 17z)" produces, and the instruction is explicit that it belongs in this box rather than beside it: "Combine this amount with any other amounts reported on line 17z to complete the line 17z entry space". It does NOT travel through /schedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxes, so unlike the Form 8621 leg it is named BOTH in the gate and in the sum, exactly as the pledge tax is. Its gate is LessThan $0 rather than GreaterThan, because a reduction is what makes this box print. The box can therefore now print a negative amount, and a return whose only 17z item is this adjustment prints it alone.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z, the printed "List type" box
Fact.Description:
The free-text half of printed Schedule 2 (Form 1040) line 17z. The printed row carries two separately addressable boxes and the instruction asks the filer to "List the type and amount of tax", so an amount printed without a type is an incomplete row.
THE FILER'S OWN ENTRY WINS WHERE THERE IS ONE. A filer who typed a type has a tax this dictionary does not compute, and their words are the ones the IRS needs to see. Where the filer typed nothing and the dictionary computed a 17z amount, the type is "HSA PLEDGE", which names the IRC 223(e)(2) / 408(e)(4) deemed distribution and is deliberately not the bare word "HSA": Schedule 2 already prints "Additional tax on HSA distributions" on line 17c, and a reader must be able to tell the two apart on the face of the form.
THE COLLISION IS A NAMED GAP RATHER THAN A SILENT CHOICE. Where the filer typed a type AND the pledge tax is positive, this box prints the filer's text alone while the amount box prints the sum of both, so the printed row understates what it is describing. This dictionary has no string-join primitive to write the filer text and "HSA PLEDGE" into one box, and inventing one for a two-box row is not this line's decision to make. The population is a filer who both pledged an HSA and owes an unrelated catch-all tax.
NO DEFAULT ARM: the box is Incomplete, and therefore blank, on a return with neither.
A FOURTH LABEL, AND THE ONLY ONE THE IRS SUPPLIES ITSELF. Where the negative Form 8978 adjustment is below $0 the row also carries "Form 8978 ADJ", which is not this dictionary's wording: both arms of the "Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet-Schedule 2 (Line 17z)" print it in parentheses as the type to list. Its gate is LessThan $0, because the amount it labels is a reduction.
THE COLLISION GAP ABOVE IS CLOSED, and a third label joins the row. The box is now a Paste of three labels separated by "; " — the filer's own text, "HSA PLEDGE", and "1294DT" for the Form 8621 section 1294 deferred tax that has become due — each an empty String when its own condition is false. Paste drops empty operands, so a row with one label prints that label alone and no stray separator. The filer's text no longer wins alone where a computed tax is also present: it prints first, followed by the computed labels, which is what the instruction's "List the type and amount of tax" asks for when the amount box carries more than one tax. The gate is unchanged in kind: with no filer text and neither computed tax positive there is still no default arm, so the box is Incomplete and prints blank.

Fact.Name: Chapter 1 taxes reported in Schedule 2 Part II, other than the negative Form 8978 adjustment
Fact.Description:
Line 1 of the "Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet-Schedule 2 (Line 17z)": "the sum of any chapter 1 taxes* (other than your negative Form 8978 adjustment) reported in Part II of Schedule 2". It is the ceiling the worksheet puts on the negative line 17z entry, and it is the whole reason that entry can never drive the chapter 1 part of Part II below zero. No printed line holds this sum; it exists only inside that worksheet.
WHAT IS IN AND WHAT IS OUT IS THE FOOTNOTE'S OWN RULE, NOT A CHOICE MADE HERE. The footnote defines chapter 1 taxes as "taxes from sections 1 through 1400Z-2 of the Code" and then names the Part II lines that generally fall outside it: 4, 7, 9, 11 through 13, 17k through 17m, and 17z. Applying both halves to this dictionary's Part II terms:
IN, each a section at or below 1400Z-2 and none of them on the excluded list. Line 8, but only its two chapter 1 legs: form5329 /form5329AdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions, the section 72(t) additional tax, and form5329 /form5329PartIiEducationAndAbleTaxOrZero, the education and ABLE distributions tax imposed by sections 529, 529A and 530. Lines 14 and 15, the section 453 and 453A installment interest. Line 16, the section 42 low income housing credit recapture. Line 17a recapture of other credits, 17b (form8828) the section 143 mortgage subsidy recapture, 17c through 17f (hsa) the section 220 and 223 additional taxes on HSA, Archer MSA and Medicare Advantage MSA distributions, 17g the section 170 fractional interest recapture, 17h section 409A, 17i section 457A, 17j section 72(m)(5), 17n the section 167 and 460 look back interest, 17o the section 871 tax on non effectively connected income, 17p and 17q the section 1291 and 1294 interest. Line 19 (form4255), the net EPE recapture.
OUT, and why each. Line 4 self employment tax, line 7 the unreported and uncollected social security and Medicare tax, line 9 household employment taxes, line 11 Additional Medicare Tax, line 12 net investment income tax and line 13 the uncollected box 12 tax are all on the footnote's excluded list, and all sit above 1400Z-2 in the Code. Line 17k golden parachute payments (section 4999), 17l tax on accumulation distribution of trusts and 17m the insider stock compensation excise tax (section 4985) are named by the footnote as excluded; 17l is the one line whose imposing section is below 1400Z-2 and the printed list excludes it anyway, so the printed list wins.
ONE DELIBERATE RESIDUAL UNDER-INCLUSION remains, in the under-claim direction and named rather than left to be discovered. LINE 17z'S UNCLASSIFIED FILER CATCH-ALL remains excluded. The footnote excludes 17z "(other than chapter 1 taxes)", so a chapter 1 item on that line belongs in this sum. A filer may now classify the adjacent catch-all amount with /writableSchedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxesIsChapter1Tax, and a complete TRUE classification is included; an unanswered or FALSE classification remains conservatively excluded. The computable hsa section 223(f)(4) pledge tax and form8621 section 1294 deferred tax are included below. The Form 5329 Part III, IV, V, VIII and IX section 4973 and 4974 excise legs of line 8 are NOT included: those sections are above 1400Z-2, so the footnote's own range leaves them out, exactly as it leaves out the HSA and Archer MSA section 4973 legs.
LINE 20 IS IN. Line 20, the section 965 net tax liability installment, is reported in Part II, section 965 lies inside the footnote's range of sections 1 through 1400Z-2, and line 20 is not on the footnote's excluded list (lines 4, 7, 9, 11 through 13, 17k through 17m and 17z). Worksheet line 1 asks for chapter 1 taxes "reported in Part II", not for the terms of line 21, so the fact that Schedule 2 line 21 does not add line 20 does not take it out of this sum. It enters through /schedule2Line20Section965NetTaxLiabilityInstallment.
NO CYCLE, AND THIS IS THE FACT WHERE ONE WOULD HAVE FORMED. Every term above is read INDIVIDUALLY. Reading /line18OfSchedule2 or taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2 instead would close a loop, because /line18OfSchedule2 now carries /schedule2Line17zNegativeForm8978Adjustment, which reads this fact. The worksheet's own parenthesis "(other than your negative Form 8978 adjustment)" is the printed form of the same requirement.
Every term resolves $0 rather than Incomplete on a return that answers none of them. The one term that can stay Incomplete is line 20 while an entered Form 965-A is not yet complete, and then the ceiling is truly unknown. /schedule2Line17zNegativeForm8978Adjustment reads this fact only when the Schedule 3 line 6l overflow is above $0, so that Incomplete reaches the tax only on a return where the worksheet applies.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z, the negative Form 8978 adjustment
Fact.Description:
The line 17z entry the "Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet-Schedule 2 (Line 17z)" produces: a NEGATIVE number, the lesser of the overflow that the Schedule 3 line 6l worksheet could not fit under its own cap and the chapter 1 taxes reported elsewhere in Schedule 2 Part II. It is the other half of a single printed routing. schedule3 /sched3Line6lWorksheetOverflowToSchedule2Line17z carries the magnitude here; this fact applies the sign and the second cap, and /line18OfSchedule2 carries it into the total.
WHY IT IS A REDUCTION AND NOT A CREDIT. The worksheet does not send the overflow to Schedule 3. Both of its arms say to list the type and an amount "as a negative number (in parentheses) on line 17z", which is Part II, other taxes. A section 6226 push out that decreases tax is therefore split by the printed forms across two places: the part that fits under Form 1040 line 18 is a nonrefundable credit on Schedule 3 line 6l, and the part above it reduces Schedule 2 other taxes instead. A filer with both an over cap adjustment and chapter 1 other taxes now gets the whole of their decrease; before this fact they got only the part under the cap.
LESSEROF IS EXACT EVEN THOUGH THE TWO WORKSHEETS ASK DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. The Schedule 3 worksheet asks whether line 1 is "equal to or more than" line 2 and this one asks whether line 1 is "more than" line 2. At equality the Yes arm gives line 2 and the No arm gives line 1, which are the same number, so the strict and non strict comparisons cannot disagree and one LesserOf serves.
THE CAP IS THE ONLY FLOOR THE INSTRUCTION PRINTS, and it is enough. Nothing in either worksheet, in the line 17z instruction, or at Schedule 2 line 21 says to floor line 18, line 21 or total tax. It does not need to: capping the negative entry at the chapter 1 taxes reported in Part II is exactly what stops the chapter 1 part of Part II going below zero. Line 18 itself CAN go negative and that is the printed arithmetic, not a defect: the ceiling counts Part II chapter 1 taxes that sit outside line 18 as well (lines 8, 14, 15, 16, 19 and 20), so a filer whose only chapter 1 tax is one of lines 8 through 19 gets a negative line 18 that line 21 then absorbs. Line 20 is the exception: line 21 does not add it, so a filer whose only chapter 1 tax is the line 20 installment can reach a line 21 below zero. That is the printed arithmetic of worksheet line 1 ("reported in Part II") and is left as printed. The one deliberate under-inclusion in the ceiling, an unclassified line 17z catch-all, is named on /schedule2PartIiChapter1TaxesExcludingNegativeForm8978Adjustment; it makes the ceiling smaller, i.e. the reduction smaller and the tax higher.
SIGN ONCE, HERE. The overflow fact holds a nonnegative magnitude because the Schedule 2 worksheet's line 2 asks for the Schedule 3 worksheet's negative line 3 "as a positive number". The single negation is applied at this entry, as Subtract from $0, so no pair of negations can quietly cancel.
GUARDED ON THE MAGNITUDE BEING POSITIVE, not merely complete. Both operands are complete safe, so an IsComplete gate alone would be vacuous; the printed worksheet is completed only when the Schedule 3 worksheet reached its line 3, which is exactly overflow greater than $0. ADDITIVE: $0 on every return that does not answer the Schedule 3 line 6l intake and on every return whose adjustment fits under Form 1040 line 18, so every committed scenario is byte identical.

Nothing in this dictionary computes it: the return this graph can represent carries no input for it, so the figure is the filer's own entry for the printed line, exactly as the four line 17 intakes already shipping in this module are. A minimum of zero applies because the printed line asks for a tax or an interest charge collected as a tax, which cannot be negative. The governing provision is IRC 4985(a); the authority comment anchors it provisionally to IRC 1. Its complete-safe wrapper /schedule2Line17mInsiderStockCompensationExciseTax is an addend of /line18OfSchedule2.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z: filer catch-all is a Chapter 1 tax (filer entry)
Fact.Description: Whether the amount entered in Schedule 2 line 17z's filer catch-all is a tax imposed by Chapter 1 (sections 1 through 1400Z-2). The printed line 17z instruction admits taxes not reported elsewhere, while the Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet requires Chapter 1 taxes on that line to be included in its ceiling. The dictionary cannot identify the section of a free-text catch-all entry, so this Boolean records the filer's classification of the adjacent amount. An unanswered classification conservatively leaves the amount out of the ceiling; it never changes the printed line 17z amount itself.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z Chapter 1 classification, or false when unanswered
Fact.Description: Complete-safe reading of /writableSchedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxesIsChapter1Tax for the Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet ceiling. An answered classification keeps its true or false value; an unanswered classification becomes false, so the adjacent catch-all amount is conservatively excluded instead of allowing an unanswered selector to fall through the chapter 1 arm.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z Chapter 1 classification is complete
Fact.Description: Complete-safe requiredness signal for the Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet ceiling. A positive filer-entered line 17z catch-all must have its adjacent Chapter 1 tax classification answered; an unanswered classification cannot safely be treated as either Chapter 1 or not Chapter 1. Returns with no positive catch-all, or with the classification answered either way, are complete. This signal feeds flow:/flowIncomplete so an unclassified positive catch-all cannot be filed while the ceiling silently omits a Chapter 1 tax. The question is required only when the Schedule 3 line 6l worksheet sends an overflow to line 17z (schedule3 /sched3Line6lWorksheetOverflowToSchedule2Line17z above $0), because the Schedule 2 worksheet is completed only then; on every other return this signal is TRUE.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17z: Any other taxes: the type (filer entry)
Fact.Description: The free text box of Schedule 2 line 17z, printed as "Any other taxes. List type and amount". The printed row carries two separately addressable boxes, this description and the amount beside it, so each gets its own fact. Nothing in this dictionary names the type or the form number the filer must list here, so it is the filer's own entry. Print only: no total reads a string. The governing provision is no Code section at all (the open residual of Part II); the authority comment anchors it provisionally to IRC 1.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 20: Section 965 net tax liability installment from Form 965-A (filer entry)

Its complete-safe wrapper /schedule2Line20Section965NetTaxLiabilityInstallment is read only by the chapter 1 ceiling of the line 17z Negative Form 8978 worksheet. See that wrapper for the reasoning.

Fact.Name: Total Form 1099-NEC box 3 excess golden parachute payments
Fact.Description: Sum of box 3 (excess golden parachute payments) over every Form 1099-NEC on the return, before applying the 20% rate, with cents intact. The amounts are read from the Form 1099-NEC document intake (scheduleC:/form1099Necs), the one intake for that box; a blank box, an empty collection or an unopened collection contributes zero. The combined Schedule 2 line 17k calculation keeps the W-2 code K tax amounts and applies 20% only to this payment total, rounding once at the line.
